question: True or false: people who only imagined straining a finger muscle, daily for four weeks, gained no measurable strength?
answer: False. In Yue and Cole's experiment, imagined maximal contractions of a little-finger muscle raised its strength by 22%, against about 30% for real contractions and under 4% for people who did neither. The muscle did not grow; the gain came from the nervous system learning to drive it harder.
move: Part of any skill lives in the signal, not the muscle.
ask: Which of my skills could I keep training in my head when I cannot practise for real?
trap: Assuming strength can only come from muscles doing real work.
reference: Guang Yue & Kelly J. Cole, Strength increases from the motor program: comparison of training with maximal voluntary and imagined muscle contractions, Journal of Neurophysiology, 1992
